archetype.name: Field General (quick-game version)
archetype.definition: A veteran who runs the offense on timing and leverage throws within 9 yards, uses under-center play-action, and saves off-script plays and deep shots for when the defense forces them.

report.headline: Efficient and protected, but the red-zone TD pace hides a thinner offense.
report.take:
This is not the 2018-2022 Mahomes who pushed the ball downfield and graded out first or near first in EPA almost every year. From 2023 to 2025 his EPA per play sat between 0.134 and 0.181, his aDOT dropped into the 6-to-8 range, and in 2025 his CPOE fell to 0.3 and his pressure-to-sack rate climbed to 28.8%. The 2026 version has adjusted to that. About three of every four attempts (95 of 128) are behind the line or within 9 yards, intended air yards are 7.1 and his throws land 1.4 yards short of the sticks. Kansas City still passes more than the situation calls for (+3.4% over expectation, 5th), but the passing is short and quick.

The adjustment is working in the places that matter most. He is pressured on just 15.2% of dropbacks, 5th lowest. His pressure-to-sack rate is back to 20% after two years near 28%. He has no fumbles, and his 8.69 adjusted net yards per dropback ranks 5th. Under center he is far better than in shotgun (0.305 vs 0.153 EPA), which fits a play-action offense built on a run game ranked 3rd in rush EPA. His work to his right has been excellent: 6.6 CPOE and 6 touchdowns on 58 throws.

The numbers hide two things. First, the touchdown rate. Nine touchdowns on 26 red-zone attempts with a +20 CPOE inside the 20 has driven his 7% TD rate. His overall CPOE (0.8, 28th) and EPA per dropback (0.192, 14th) say he has been a good quarterback, not a dominant one. Second, the middle of the field. There he is at -0.091 EPA with -8 CPOE and both interceptions. He has also completed 38.9% of deep balls, with two picks on 18 tries. The deep EPA (0.355) is propped up by Tyquan Thornton, whose 1.269 EPA per target on 15 looks was the offense's big-play outlet. Thornton is now out three to four months after ankle surgery.

Where this goes depends on who replaces those vertical snaps. Xavier Worthy has 22 targets at -0.152 EPA per target. Travis Kelce (0.744) and Rashee Rice (0.217, hamstring, expected back after the bye) carry the efficiency. Expect the short game to hold up. Expect the touchdown pace to cool, and the weeks against good defenses to look like Week 4 against Las Vegas (ranked 2nd). In that game he held the ball 3.04 seconds, threw into tight windows 20% of the time and completed half his passes.

strengths.title: Protection and pressure management restored
strengths.body: He has been pressured on only 15.2% of dropbacks, and pressure becomes a sack 20% of the time. That is a clear recovery from 27.3% in 2024 and 28.8% in 2025. A 2.7-second time to throw and a quick-game structure are doing much of the work, along with a team hit rate allowed that ranks 8th. It should hold as long as the offense stays short, though it will be tested by better pass rushes.

strengths.title: Short-area timing and play-action
strengths.body: On 63 throws of 0-9 air yards he has produced 0.302 EPA with 6 touchdowns and no interceptions. Under center he posts 0.305 EPA and 58.8% success. A strong run game makes the play-action threat real. This is the most sustainable part of his profile, because it rests on scheme and on Kelce, not on explosive plays.

strengths.title: Still efficient when it is close
strengths.body: On 22 dropbacks in close fourth quarters he has 0.435 EPA and two touchdowns. His eight scrambles have each added 0.445 EPA, with four first downs. The sample is small, but late-game command and well-chosen scrambles have been part of his game for years.

concerns.title: Red-zone touchdown rate will regress
concerns.body: All nine passing touchdowns have come in the red zone, on 26 attempts with a +20 CPOE. That accuracy is far above his 0.8 overall CPOE and is not a repeatable baseline. His 7% TD rate is running well ahead of what his efficiency supports, so expect closer to one to two touchdowns a game.

concerns.title: Losing the vertical outlet
concerns.body: Thornton was the one receiver turning deep shots into points, at 1.269 EPA per target. He is out until around January. Worthy, the next downfield option, has been below zero per target. Without Thornton, his 38.9% deep completion rate and two deep interceptions could turn the deep game from volatile but positive into a drain.

concerns.title: Middle of the field and accuracy
concerns.body: Throws over the middle have gone badly: -0.091 EPA, -8 CPOE and both interceptions. The accuracy dip that began in 2025 (CPOE 0.3, 34th) has carried into this season, and in Weeks 1 and 4 his CPOE was double-digit and high-single-digit negative. This looks like a real multi-year trait rather than four-game noise, even though the middle split is only 33 throws.

trend.note: His game EPA went -2.3, +13.4, +12.9, +1.7. The two strong games came against bottom-10 defenses (IND, MIA). Against Las Vegas, now ranked 2nd, he had to hold the ball longer and throw into tight windows, and the efficiency dropped.

nextGame.headline: Off the bye against a pass rush that will test the quick game
nextGame.body:
The Chargers are the strongest pass rush he has faced. They rank 3rd in hit rate and 6th in sack rate, which goes straight at the one part of his game that has rebounded. The coverage behind that rush is beatable: 25th in explosive pass rate allowed, 20th in deep EPA allowed and 16th in pass EPA. Quarterbacks have managed only 236.5 yards a game against them (10th fewest), but that partly reflects game script. The Chargers' offense is 31st in EPA and passes 9 points below expectation, which shortens games and limits possessions. Kansas City is home, in a division game, on 14 days of rest.

Availability cuts both ways. On his side, Thornton is gone, so the deep shots now go to Worthy. Rice's hamstring is described as minor, with a return date that matches this game; if he plays, Mahomes gets back his best intermediate target behind Kelce. Josh Simmons is listed out but hasn't played this year, so the line is unchanged. On the Chargers' side, Derwin James was week-to-week with a hamstring. If he misses, the middle of the field, where Mahomes has struggled, gets easier. Donte Jackson (CB, questionable) and Dalvin Tomlinson (DT, out as of last report) are also worth checking. The Chargers' offensive line is in worse shape, with Slater out four to six weeks and Alt questionable. Kansas City's defense, though, ranks only 31st in sack rate, so it may not be able to take advantage.

keyMatchups.title: Chiefs protection versus Chargers hit rate
keyMatchups.body: He has been pressured on just 15.2% of dropbacks. The Chargers hit opposing quarterbacks at the 3rd-highest rate and sack them at the 6th-highest. If the quick game holds up, the sack issue stays fixed. If not, the 2024-25 version returns.

keyMatchups.title: Explosive passes without Thornton
keyMatchups.body: The Chargers give up explosive passes at a 9.7% rate (25th) and 0.543 EPA on deep throws. That is an opening, but the receiver who cashed those chances is out. Whether Worthy can turn deep targets into positive plays decides whether Kansas City can attack this weakness.

keyMatchups.title: A shortened game script
keyMatchups.body: The Chargers run far more than expected (-9 pass rate over expectation) and have a bottom-two offense, so expect fewer possessions. If Kansas City leads early, its 3rd-ranked run game should take more of the snaps.

nextGame.watch: Who gets the deep and intermediate targets now that Thornton is out, and whether Rice is active to take some of them.

restOfSeason.body:
The short-passing foundation should hold: low pressure, a sack rate back near his career norm, and an efficient run game that keeps play-action working. That points to steady EPA around 0.15-0.20 per dropback. Expect some regression in two places. The red-zone touchdown pace on 26 attempts will cool. The deep game also loses its most efficient receiver, which will make the explosive-play rate depend more on Rice's health and Worthy's development.

Overall, expect a good but not top-five quarterback in efficiency, with more yardage swings against strong defenses. His touchdown totals should settle closer to his 2023-2025 rates than his 2.25-a-game start. The 2025 accuracy dip has carried into this season, and interceptions over the middle are the main downside risk.
swingFactors: Rice's hamstring and who replaces Thornton's vertical role
Whether pass protection holds up against top pass rushes

bets.reason: All nine touchdowns came on a +20 CPOE in the red zone, which won't hold. The Chargers' run-heavy, 31st-ranked offense should also limit Kansas City's possessions.

Quarterbacks have averaged only 236.5 yards against the Chargers (10th fewest), and Kansas City lost its most efficient downfield receiver. A possible Kansas City lead behind a 3rd-ranked run game also points to fewer late dropbacks.

The Chargers' offense is 31st in EPA, passes 9 points below expectation and is missing two starting linemen, which means slow, run-heavy drives. No total is posted yet, so check it against the 42.5-47.5 range of his games so far.

confidence.note: Four games, two of them against bottom-10 defenses, and the receiving group just changed with Thornton out and Rice uncertain. The multi-year career trends help anchor the read.
